## Overview

The Mayo, or Yoreme, are an Indigenous group in Mexico living in southern Sonora, northern Sinaloa, and small settlements in Durango. They originally lived near the Mayo River and Fuerte River valleys. Approximately 40,000 people speak Mayo, an Uto-Aztecan language belonging to the Cahita branch and closely related to Yaqui. The Mayo sustain themselves mainly through agriculture and fishing, while also producing artwork, handicrafts, and other crafts. Their culture includes elected traditional authorities, agricultural and fishing practices, adobe and wood houses, religious festivals, and a flag depicting a deer surrounded by stars.

## Material culture

### Architecture

Mayo houses are built from adobe or wood, depending on the climate and location.

## Music & performance

## Festivals & rituals

The principal Mayo festival takes place during Easter and portrays the passion of Christ. Other festivals celebrate St. Juan Bautista, St. Francis of Assisi, and the Virgin of Guadalupe.

## Foodways

The Mayo sustain themselves mainly through agriculture and fishing. The sources state that the earliest inhabitants hunted, fished, and gathered plants, and later developed an agricultural technique that enabled settlement in different communities. Contemporary Mayo people farm, often using advanced techniques, and fish.

## Language & religion

Mayo, known natively as *Yorem Noki*, is an Uto-Aztecan language spoken by about 40,000 Mayo people in southern Sonora and northern Sinaloa. It belongs to the Cahita branch and is closely related to Yaqui; the two languages are partially intelligible. Mayo is described as critically endangered by UNESCO and is recognized in Mexico as a national language alongside other Indigenous languages and Spanish. It is agglutinative, using suffix complexes for various purposes, and its alphabet includes a, b, c, ch, e, gu, hu, i, j, l, m, n, o, p, qu, r, s, t, u, y, and ’. Mayo traditional authorities are elected by vote, and their hierarchy is respected on par with Mexican civil laws. Mayo festivals include the Christian observances of Easter and celebrations of St. Juan Bautista, St. Francis of Assisi, and the Virgin of Guadalupe.
